rv.q: Oh, and it's got a performance from Cate Blanchett that may well be the best of the year.

It’s a dazzling performance at the heart of a superbly acted production bristling with wit, compassion and intelligence, playfully reframing Chekhov’s 1895 drama about fame, love and the meaning of art for our turbulent times.
Time and again, The Seagull is an engine for extraordinary performances.
Ostermeier’s production is full of devices that could feel gimmicky if they didn’t clearly come from an intimate understanding of Chekhov’s play.
Happily, she stops the rot. But, to be fair, that is thanks in large part to a remarkable ensemble of home-grown talent.
It is the director's terror of being conventional that becomes so irritating. By the end, this version of The Seagull has become a half-dead parrot.
For those of us in the sceptical camp, it’s a little like seeing a classic rewritten with children’s crayons, even if Blanchett’s casting has turned the venture into the hottest of hot tickets.
This is, hands down, the funniest Seagull I’ve ever seen.
It’s all perfectly poised and deep.

cn.t: Mostly rapturous reviews for Ostermeier's bold, self-referential Chekhov, with Blanchett earning particular praise. A few critics find the modern trappings gimmicky, but the ensemble acting and sharp wit win most over.
